video_title: Training Camp Media Availability | October 5, 2026 | OKC Thunder

quotes.speaker: Shai Gilgeous-Alexander
quotes.summary_phrase: Shai Gilgeous-Alexander on his improved conditioning and versatility
quotes.excerpt: I feel like I'm a better basketball player, more versatile as a basketball player, and better shape too.
quotes.quote: I feel like I'm a better basketball player, more versatile as a basketball player, and better shape too. I would say those two things, my versatility offensively and defensively, and better shape.
quotes.social_post: Shai Gilgeous-Alexander says he is entering the season in better shape and more versatile on both ends of the floor. He says I feel like I am a better basketball player.

quotes.speaker: Shai Gilgeous-Alexander
quotes.summary_phrase: Shai Gilgeous-Alexander on the team's focus during training camp
quotes.excerpt: This group especially, we understand what it takes to win. We know what it's going to look like.
quotes.quote: This group especially, we understand what it takes to win. We know what it's going to look like, whether it's in the middle of January or the middle of June. We know what it takes to win. It's just about how fast can we get to that, how fast can we be on the same page, how fast can we get our communication firing, and how fast can we implement the things that we've learned from last season.
quotes.social_post: Shai Gilgeous-Alexander on the Thunder mindset heading into the season. He says this group understands what it takes to win and the focus is on how fast they can get to that level of execution.

quotes.speaker: Shai Gilgeous-Alexander
quotes.summary_phrase: Shai Gilgeous-Alexander on his post-practice workout routine
quotes.excerpt: I usually work out post-practice, especially in training camp, just because the games are still a little ways away.
quotes.quote: I usually work out post-practice, especially in training camp, just because the games are still a little ways away and I can empty my tank. It's a little bit hard to do so when you have a game every other day during the season.
quotes.social_post: Shai Gilgeous-Alexander explains why he pushes his conditioning during training camp. He says I usually work out post-practice because the games are still a little ways away and I can empty my tank.

quotes.speaker: Shai Gilgeous-Alexander
quotes.summary_phrase: Shai Gilgeous-Alexander on his growth as a leader and father
quotes.excerpt: It's grown for sure. It's something that I've been intentional with, but also naturally it's just grown because I've grown as a man.
quotes.quote: It's grown for sure. It's something that I've been intentional with, but also naturally it's just grown because I've grown as a man. Becoming a father has helped with that. You're an example for somebody every day, and that's a little bit different in the real world, but it's essentially the same thing. You lead by example, and it's hard to get people to follow you if you don't do the right things and walk the walk.
quotes.social_post: Shai Gilgeous-Alexander reflects on his growth as a leader. He says becoming a father has helped him lead by example because you are an example for somebody every day.

quotes.speaker: Shai Gilgeous-Alexander
quotes.summary_phrase: Shai Gilgeous-Alexander on learning from last season's playoff injuries
quotes.excerpt: Don't make any excuses and be ready for whatever the cards you get dealt.
quotes.quote: Obviously the injuries last year were unfortunate and you can't prepare for them. I wasn't prepared for those things to happen and I think it bit me in the butt. So for me, it was don't make any excuses and be ready for whatever the cards you get dealt. So if two of your best ball-handlers go down, being in good enough shape, being as versatile as you can be on both ends of the floor to be able to handle that and carry the same load regardless of what's going on.
quotes.social_post: Shai Gilgeous-Alexander on learning from last year's playoff injuries. He says I was not prepared for those things to happen and it bit me in the butt so I am focused on being ready for whatever cards I get dealt.

quotes.speaker: Shai Gilgeous-Alexander
quotes.summary_phrase: Shai Gilgeous-Alexander on Russell Westbrook's impact on the Thunder
quotes.excerpt: The foundation for what we stand on now, part of the reason why this city is what it is.
quotes.quote: His dynamic is they come in terms of NBA player, personality, teammate, he's the whole package. The foundation for what we stand on now, part of the reason why this city is what it is is because of Russell Westbrook, and he deserves all those flowers for what he's done off the court and on the court. It's obviously a little shocking that it's this soon, I feel like he had a little bit more in the tank, but everyone has their own journey.
quotes.social_post: Shai Gilgeous-Alexander on Russell Westbrook. He says the foundation for what the Thunder stand on is because of him and admits it is a little shocking that his career is at this stage as he feels he had more in the tank.

quotes.speaker: Mark Daigneault
quotes.summary_phrase: Mark Daigneault on Ousmane Dieng's development and athleticism
quotes.excerpt: He's got kind of an electric athleticism. He's one of those players that kind of makes things happen.
quotes.quote: Ousmane Dieng has done a good job. He obviously got hurt in Summer League, so we didn't get an extended look at him then, but he's got kind of an electric athleticism. He's one of those players that kind of makes things happen. His offensive rebounds, he runs the floor, he's a physical driver, he's got a great athletic profile, and so just like the rest of the young players this year and in past years, it becomes about his ability to pick up the fundamental stuff that shows up every possession.
quotes.social_post: Mark Daigneault praises Ousmane Dieng for his electric athleticism. He says Dieng has a great athletic profile and the focus now is on his ability to pick up the fundamental stuff that shows up every possession.

quotes.speaker: Mark Daigneault
quotes.summary_phrase: Mark Daigneault on building good habits and avoiding shortcuts
quotes.excerpt: We can't win a game right now, we can't make the playoffs right now.
quotes.quote: Some of it is trusting the maturity and competitiveness of the guys and them understanding the paces that you have to go through to prepare yourself for the season. We can't win a game right now, we can't make the playoffs right now. All we can do is have quality practices and stack quality days up and build our habits, and this team has done an exceptional job in the past of understanding that and putting the work in, not cutting corners.
quotes.social_post: Mark Daigneault on the Thunder approach to training camp. He says we cannot win a game right now so all we can do is have quality practices and stack quality days up and build our habits.

quotes.speaker: Mark Daigneault
quotes.summary_phrase: Mark Daigneault on the importance of veteran leadership in training camp
quotes.excerpt: It's important to take the rep in front of you in practice or being in the pick-and-roll coverage.
quotes.quote: Our exhibits have been outstanding. Alex Caruso is obviously a more veteran player, he's been in training camps before, he's played in the NBA, the other guys are younger, but it's important to take the rep in front of you in practice or being in the pick-and-roll coverage with Cason Wallace or having Jared McCain talking to you about transition defense. He's the guy back talking, he's really good at that, that certainly helps them because it plugs them into a functional environment where the people around them are doing the job.
quotes.social_post: Mark Daigneault highlights the impact of Alex Caruso on the younger players. He says Caruso is a veteran who helps plug the younger guys into a functional environment where people around them are doing the job.

quotes.speaker: Mark Daigneault
quotes.summary_phrase: Mark Daigneault on the limitations of Summer League data
quotes.excerpt: Summer League is an important data point, but it's also wildly out of context.
quotes.quote: It's more of a commentary on not overreacting to Summer League, because Summer League is an important data point, but it's also wildly out of context. It's right after the draft, they've been on site for less than a week, they're exhausted from the draft process, and then the game context is totally different. There's 10 fouls, there's four 10-minute quarters, it couldn't be more different from this time. So you definitely get a better sense, in both directions, you can have a guy play really well in that context then struggle in this one and vice versa.
quotes.social_post: Mark Daigneault warns against overreacting to Summer League. He says it is an important data point but it is also wildly out of context compared to the real NBA game.
